cards.front: Complete the rule: Obey signals and roadway markings unless a police.
cards.back: Obey signals and roadway markings unless a police or traffic-control officer directs otherwise, and never leave the road to evade a signal.
cards.memory_hook: Officer direction can override signal

cards.front: Complete the rule: A typical three-color traffic signal orders red, yellow.
cards.back: A typical three-color traffic signal orders red, yellow and green from top to bottom or left to right.
cards.memory_hook: Red yellow green in standard sequence

cards.front: Complete the rule: A nonworking intersection signal requires an all-way stop.
cards.back: A nonworking intersection signal requires an all-way stop, then observation and yielding before entry, unless police direct another action.
cards.memory_hook: Dark signal becomes all way stop

cards.front: Complete the rule: At a red signal, stop before the marked.
cards.back: At a red signal, stop before the marked line, otherwise before the crosswalk or intersection, and wait for green and a clear intersection unless making a permitted red-light turn.
cards.memory_hook: Red requires stop at proper location

cards.front: Complete the rule: After a full stop and yielding to pedestrians.
cards.back: After a full stop and yielding to pedestrians and approaching traffic, a right turn on red is allowed unless a sign prohibits it.
cards.memory_hook: Right on red requires stop yield

cards.front: Complete the rule: A left turn on red is allowed from.
cards.back: A left turn on red is allowed from a one-way street onto a one-way street carrying traffic leftward after stopping and yielding.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A steady yellow warns that green is changing.
cards.back: A steady yellow warns that green is changing to red, and the driver must not enter once red appears.
cards.memory_hook: Yellow announces ending green

cards.front: Complete the rule: A green signal permits movement only after yielding.
cards.back: A green signal permits movement only after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the crossing or intersection.
cards.memory_hook: Green still yields to occupied crossing

cards.front: Complete the rule: At a flashing red intersection signal, stop, yield.
cards.back: At a flashing red intersection signal, stop, yield to traffic in the intersection or crosswalk and proceed only when safe.
cards.memory_hook: Flashing red follows stop and yield

cards.front: Complete the rule: A flashing yellow intersection.
cards.back: A flashing yellow intersection light allows proceeding cautiously.
cards.memory_hook: Flashing yellow means caution

cards.front: Complete the rule: Movement in a traffic arrow’s direction still requires.
cards.back: Movement in a traffic arrow’s direction still requires yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection or crosswalk.
cards.memory_hook: Arrow direction still respects occupied crossing

cards.front: Complete the rule: A steady red arrow generally forbids its indicated.
cards.back: A steady red arrow generally forbids its indicated movement, but the handbook allows a right turn or the stated one-way-to-one-way left turn after a full stop and yielding.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A steady yellow arrow warns that a green.
cards.back: A steady yellow arrow warns that a green arrow is ending or that the signal will soon turn red.
cards.memory_hook: Steady yellow arrow ends protected interval

cards.front: Complete the rule: A flashing yellow arrow allows a turn in.
cards.back: A flashing yellow arrow allows a turn in its direction after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection or crosswalk.
cards.memory_hook: Flashing yellow arrow permits yielded turn

cards.front: Complete the rule: A green arrow pointing up allows straight travel.
cards.back: A green arrow pointing up allows straight travel only, while a right- or left-pointing arrow permits the indicated turn.
cards.memory_hook: Green arrow limits movement to shown

cards.front: Complete the rule: A pedestrian facing a walking-person signal.
cards.back: A pedestrian facing a walking-person signal may cross in the signal’s direction.
cards.memory_hook: Walking person signal permits directed crossing

cards.front: Complete the rule: A flashing orange raised hand means do not.
cards.back: A flashing orange raised hand means do not begin crossing, but someone who began under a steady walking signal may finish to the sidewalk or safety island.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A steady orange raised hand.
cards.back: A steady orange raised hand means do not enter the roadway.
cards.memory_hook: Steady hand means no new entry

cards.front: Complete the rule: An overhead red cross means.
cards.back: An overhead red cross means the lane cannot be used.
cards.memory_hook: Red lane cross closes lane

cards.front: Complete the rule: An overhead yellow cross warns of a coming.
cards.back: An overhead yellow cross warns of a coming red cross, so leave the lane safely before it turns red.
cards.memory_hook: Yellow lane cross requires safe exit

cards.front: Complete the rule: The handbook’s flashing yellow overhead arrow identifies a.
cards.back: The handbook’s flashing yellow overhead arrow identifies a lane available for approaching and making a left turn.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A green lane arrow permits lane use.
cards.back: A green lane arrow permits lane use subject to all other traffic signs and signals.
cards.memory_hook: Green lane arrow does not override

cards.front: Complete the rule: A solid white edge line marks the road’s.
cards.back: A solid white edge line marks the road’s right boundary, while a solid yellow line marks the left edge of a divided roadway.
cards.memory_hook: Edge line color distinguishes road side

cards.front: Complete the rule: White lane lines divide lanes.
cards.back: White lane lines divide lanes traveling in the same direction.
cards.memory_hook: White separates same direction traffic

cards.front: Complete the rule: A broken white line may be.
cards.back: A broken white line may be crossed to change lanes or turn.
cards.memory_hook: Broken white permits specified crossing

cards.front: Complete the rule: Crossing a single solid white lane.
cards.back: Crossing a single solid white lane line is discouraged and requires special caution.
cards.memory_hook: Single solid white discourages crossing

cards.front: Complete the rule: Crossing a double solid.
cards.back: Crossing a double solid white lane boundary is prohibited.
cards.memory_hook: Double solid white prohibits crossing

cards.front: Complete the rule: Yellow center markings separate.
cards.back: Yellow center markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A solid yellow line on your side marks.
cards.back: A solid yellow line on your side marks a no-passing area, but it may be crossed to finish a pass begun before the area or to make the stated left-access turn.

cards.back: With one broken and one solid yellow center line, passing is allowed only from the side nearest the broken line.
cards.memory_hook: Broken line side determines passing permission

cards.front: Complete the rule: A two-way left-turn lane is identified by yellow.
cards.back: A two-way left-turn lane is identified by yellow lines and white arrows, and left turns must use that lane when it is provided.
cards.memory_hook: Provided center turn lane is required

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use a two-way left-turn lane only to prepare.
cards.back: Use a two-way left-turn lane only to prepare for or make a left turn into or out of the road, or a lawful U-turn.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A white transverse stop line marks where a.
cards.back: A white transverse stop line marks where a red light or stop sign requires stopping, with every part of the vehicle remaining behind the line.

cards.front: Complete the rule: In urban areas the stop line.

cards.memory_hook: Stop line generally precedes urban crosswalk

cards.memory_hook: White crossing markings identify pedestrian priority

cards.front: Complete the rule: A marked crossing can be in the middle.

cards.back: Diagonal yellow or white stripes mark fixed obstructions, and solid white or yellow lines can guide traffic around a hazard.

cards.back: A solid yellow line before a railway crossing prohibits passing, and white stop lines indicate where to stop for a train.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Automated crossing enforcement can record the plate, location.
cards.back: Automated crossing enforcement can record the plate, location and time of a violation, which can bring fines and possible license suspension.
cards.memory_hook: Crossing violation can be recorded automatically

cards.front: Complete the rule: An emergency-notification sign identifies the railroad’s contact information.
cards.back: An emergency-notification sign identifies the railroad’s contact information and the specific crossing so the public can report an emergency to the responsible railroad.
